Visual Design.assessment:
# Cycle 47 — Visual Design Reviewer

**APPROVE.** The compiled preview confines the overflow fade to the moving certificate links in LTR and RTL. All three pinned row labels and both short status values retain their full theme ink throughout the pan.

## Independent inspection

I opened the frozen port 47963 build in Chrome and compared it with the accepted port 47851 baseline and cycle 46 on port 47855. I inspected the Home table at its start, midpoint and end, single and rapid refresh, graph launcher and modal, mobile Explorer, Blog listing, keyboard-selected Azure search result, Linux disk article table, and Azure prose and fenced PowerShell. I covered 390×844, 900×900 and 1440×900 in light and pure-black dark, including RTL set before initial document layout. I inspected the twelve paired table and context sheets and produced the three-version phone comparison. [Baseline, cycle 46 and cycle 47 in RTL](rtl-phone.webp).

## Findings

- **Fade and pinned labels.** I captured 36 matched table states across both directions, both themes, three sizes and three positions. I then disabled the mask in the same browser state for a diagnostic image difference. All 24 active fades changed pixels only in the certificate link cell. All 12 inactive states produced identical images. At 390px in the dark theme the visible fade occupied x=328–354 in LTR and x=250–277 immediately beside the pinned column in RTL. The “o” that faded from #f5f5f5 to #303030 in cycle 46 retained #f5f5f5 in every dark state and #141413 in every light state. The two status rows had zero changed pixels in all 36 diagnostics.
- **Keyboard and refresh.** Forward and reverse Tab through the ten certificates produced 120 checks across both directions and all widths. Every link’s full outline fit and every center hit the focused anchor. The settled LTR captures retained the original 418px, 128px and 97px end positions after ordinary and fast reloads. An initial phone double-refresh run landed 4px short with the final certificate and both statuses still readable. Eight dedicated repeats with 20–200ms between reloads all restored the exact 418px endpoint, including after an additional settling period. This isolated variation has no material visual impact. RTL middle and end restoration also passed, including the script-disabled sticky status fallback.
- **Graph and motion.** Desktop Home rendered one local and one open global canvas on initial, ordinary and rapid loads in default Chrome and with WebGL disabled. The wide launcher regained focus on Escape. Tablet showed its graph below the content, desktop in its rail, and phone omitted it. Reduced motion at first paint and after a live preference change removed the visible graph and its canvas. Graph colors and page backgrounds kept their established warm light and pure-black dark treatments.
- **Typography and surroundings.** Home’s table text retained its 14px SN Pro treatment. Source Serif 4 prose measured 16.175px, 17.45px and 18px at the three widths. Azure fenced code used TX-02 at 14.5px/22px. The Blog listing, selected search result, mobile navigation, reading column and article table kept their original hierarchy and spacing. The matched Linux table crops were pixel-identical at 900px and 1440px; at 390px the changed pixels were confined to its existing 28px overflow cue.
- **Scope and maintainability.** The correction in `quartz/styles/custom.scss` targets the Home link-bearing cell in either reading direction. It shares the existing fade declarations with ordinary article tables and stops depending on direction selectors transformed by the production compiler. The status spans and scrolling behavior remain local to the Home table. I found no critical or material visual defect.

Responsive and Accessibility.assessment:
# Cycle 47 · Responsive and Accessibility Reviewer

**APPROVE.** The built site fixes the fading RTL row headers and keeps the last certificate’s text, icon and focus ring together. I found no material responsive or accessibility regression.

- **Rendered ink.** I compared the accepted and candidate table and context sheets for all six combinations of 390×844, 900×900 and 1440×900 with light and pure-black dark themes, plus the separate RTL phone comparison with cycle 46. I independently captured the actual Home at start, midpoint and end in both directions. The counts of high-contrast pixels in all three header labels were identical before and after panning in every one of the 12 width/theme/direction combinations. At 390px RTL the light counts were 214/239/97 for Obtained/In Progress/Todo at each position. In dark they were 238/259/112. The link-cell fade is visible beside the pinned heading. The built browser rule leaves the table and all row headings unmasked.
- **Keyboard and contrast.** On the initialized table, I tested 520 forward and reverse focus stops across directions, themes, widths, RTL starting offsets and forced-colors samples. Every certificate's text, external icon and 2px focus ring was visible (within a half-pixel of geometric rounding). The link’s text center hit the focused anchor. Keyboard focus removed the fade. Shift+Tab onto AZ-900 on the RTL phone now brings the entire link into view. Table text uses SN Pro 14px, with 17.50:1 light contrast and 19.26:1 on pure black. The normal-theme focus ring measures 13.00:1 light and 15.61:1 dark. In forced colors the system-drawn outline remained visible.
- **Restoration and reflow.** At all widths the CAISP and Todo values stayed beside the corresponding labels throughout panning and after reload. Ordinary end-position and rapid-double midpoint reload samples yielded 430/215, 128/64 and 97/49px LTR, and −430/−215, −128/−64 and −97/−48px RTL. Fresh JavaScript-disabled checks at all three widths and all three positions preserved both short values in both directions. Firefox native zoom at 100%, 200% and 400% produced 1280, 640 and 320 CSS-pixel viewports and preserved reading and local scrolling in both themes.
- **Surroundings.** I navigated Home, Blog, the Azure Machine Configuration article and the Linux disk article in the live build, inspected the paired screen captures, and exercised Search, mobile Explorer, SPA navigation, graph dialog and reduced-motion changes. Search and Explorer returned focus to their openers. On tablet and desktop, graph Close received focus, Tab stayed in the dialog and Escape restored the trigger. Switching an open graph to reduced motion removed both canvases and moved focus to the site title. Restoring motion yielded one local canvas. Phone graph canvases were absent. Paragraphs used Source Serif 4, fenced code used TX-02 at 14.5px, and the wider Linux table scrolled inside its wrapper without page overflow.
- **Maintenance.** Limiting the Home mask to its scrolling certificate-link cell works in either direction without relying on language or on a compiler rewrite of the direction selector. The generic article-table fade and Home’s existing semantics are preserved.

Paired evidence is under `design-evidence/refresh-repair/cycle-47/`, including `rtl-phone.webp`. My raw browser and pixel measurements are under `/tmp/quartz-refresh-repair/`: `fourth-access.json`, `47963-access-ink-stats.json`, `47963-access-settledkeys.json`, `47963-access-native-zoom.json`, `47963-access-nojs{,-rtl}.json` and `47963-access-motion.json`.

CSS and Quartz V5.assessment:
# Cycle 47 · CSS and Quartz V5 review

**Decision — APPROVE** for the stylesheet and Quartz behavior. The previously obscured RTL headings remain readable with the cue active. No critical or material regression found.

## Changes and coverage

Compared the cycle 46 stylesheet with the frozen cycle 47 source and inspected the selectors in the CSS served on port 47963 (`index-b597f345.css`, `postscript-a4122608.js`). Reviewed the six baseline/candidate table sheets, six surrounding-page sheets and RTL phone comparison in `design-evidence/refresh-repair/cycle-47`. Reopened Home after inspecting the comparisons. The six full Chrome 158 runs used 390 × 844, 900 × 900 and 1440 × 900 in light and pure-black dark themes. Inspected Home, the 56-entry Blog listing, Azure search and arrow-key selection, mobile Explorer, SPA navigation, the nine-row Linux article table, Azure Machine Configuration article code, local/global graphs and reduced-motion transitions.

## Cascade, pixels and responsiveness

- The compiled generic rule excludes the certification table by class, while the certification branch applies its mask to the linked cell. Both share the overflow, screen, forced-colors and keyboard-focus conditions. The production output retains these selectors without language or direction translation. No script state, another color token, theme override, or dependency is required.
- Independently captured each live midpoint with its normal mask and with just that mask disabled. All 12 pixel pairs across direction, size and theme changed only the obtained-links row. None changed a pinned header or a status row. In the 390 px crop the affected band was x316–342 for LTR and x238–265 for RTL, placing it at the visible boundary of the links in each direction. At 900 and 1440 px the largest affected band was 28 px. The prior cycle faded the pinned column. Evidence in `/tmp/quartz-refresh-repair/css47-edge-scope.json` and the corresponding `css47-*-live.png` / `css47-*-none.png` captures.
- All 24 active-cue scope checks produced a mask only on the linked cell, including root LTR, root RTL, article ancestor RTL and CSS-only article direction. Forced colors cleared both cell and table masks in all six size/theme combinations. Physical right-edge overflow cleared at the actual physical end. The ordinary article table still masked as a table when it overflowed on the phone and fit without a cue on the wider layouts.
- All 38 forward/backward keyboard samples in the two directions kept focus and link text visible, including AZ-900. The CSS fallback kept the short statuses visible with JavaScript disabled. Normal and double refresh restored 430/128/97 px in the three independent configurations. At 125% zoom and DPR 1.25 the browser restored the full 508.80 px endpoint. The 150% check also kept status text visible. Table typography remained SN Pro; code remained 14.5 px TX-02. Warm light and pure-black reader surfaces, navigation and graph inks matched the baseline.

## Quartz behavior, maintenance and validation

The stylesheet change reuses the existing scroll cue and measured hidden distance and preserves the registry and renderer lifecycle. The media-conditioned graph stayed absent on phone. Both global dismissal paths returned focus to the trigger on tablet and desktop. Motion changes settled at zero and then one local canvas. The separately held global close/reopen test recorded two distinct live renderers while open, one after dismissal and zero uncaught Pixi errors. Build and all 167 unit tests passed. The frozen type-check log records the same two baseline declaration errors for micromorph and remark-parse. These are repository check results for the director to reconcile separately from this CSS assessment.

No further design correction or stylistic preference recorded.

designDirector.assessment:
## Cycle 47 · APPROVE

Visual Design, Responsive and Accessibility, and CSS and Quartz V5 each independently approved the frozen production build. I approve cycle 47 for the local implementation. The correction moved the Home overflow fade into the moving certificate-link cell for both directions and removed the compiler-sensitive language dependency. The generic article-table cue still works. The scroll region retains its name, all ten certificates remain navigable, and the status text is available even with JavaScript disabled.

My 390px Chrome measurements on the emitted site preserved the full 430px LTR and −430px RTL endpoints through an ordinary refresh and an immediate double refresh in both themes. CAISP remained visible at the beginning, middle, end and both reloads. Reverse Tab brought the visible AZ-900 text into focus and cleared the mask in all four runs. Comparing each actual midpoint against the identical state with the mask disabled located every changed pixel within the first row: a 27px-wide LTR band and a 28px-wide RTL band immediately beside the pinned column. The earlier RTL captures carried changed pixels through all three row headings. Wider-layout sheets, native zoom, forced colors and all 520 settled keyboard checks corroborate the repair.

One light-phone run landed at 414px against a 418px endpoint after a double refresh. All text and the last credential remained visible. Eight dedicated repeats with 20–200ms gaps measured 418px both on reload and after further settling. The Chrome, Brave, WebKit and Firefox table results, 24 fractional-zoom cases, and separate font-loading cases support classifying the isolated four-pixel observation as minor. No critical or material regression remains.

I opened and dismissed the desktop graph after first load, ordinary refresh and double refresh in Chrome with WebGL disabled. The candidate kept one local canvas, an active global canvas while open, and returned focus after dismissal in all three runs. The previous build missed its local canvas within 2.5 seconds after both reload attempts in that comparison. Chrome and Brave stress results also confirm surviving graphs retain their resources during overlapping creation, and that media changes remove renderers, tickers and simulations. The design retains the established graph palette, editorial typography, TX-02 code, and pure-black dark background.

The local production build emitted 913 files. All 167 automated tests passed; the changed-file formatting check, whitespace check and 252-route integrity comparison passed. The full checker reproduced the baseline dependency declaration diagnostics for micromorph and remark-parse/lib. The GitHub Pages workflow for this repository requires the production build, and the full-check workflow is restricted to the upstream Quartz repository.

Frozen final asset: index-b597f345.css and postscript-a4122608.js. The three final assessments are in /tmp/quartz-refresh-repair/fourth-{visual,access,css}-review.md. My captures and measurements are in /tmp/quartz-refresh-repair/director-browser. The paired table, surrounding-page and RTL comparison sheets are in design-evidence/refresh-repair/cycle-47, with the consolidated automation and integrity results in design-evidence/refresh-repair/validation.json.
